prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is a clear mechanistic principle: a small molecule brings a chosen protein and an E3 ligase together so that the cell's own ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes the target instead of merely inhibiting it. That changes what is druggable and is a genuinely new capability. It can be explained to a broad audience, it is chemistry-centred, and the concept has been reproduced by many independent groups and is now reaching late-stage trials. After listening to colleagues I have moved my third name from Ciulli to Handa. Three colleagues (Aili, Aqvist, Chabes) independently named Handa. His identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target (2010) gave a precise molecular explanation for a drug already in the clinic and underpins the glue branch, while Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs (2001). Together they give a citation that covers the full principle rather than one modality.
statement.case_against: Clinical proof is still maturing, since no PROTAC drug is clearly approved as far as I know, so the prize could be early. Credit is also crowded: Sakamoto, Ciulli, Ito, Kim and Gray all have real claims, and any three-person cut will exclude someone whose contribution was essential to making degraders drug-like, especially Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures. Merging the PROTAC and cereblon-glue stories into a single citation also risks combining two discoveries made by different groups at different times.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with pKa-tuned lipid design giving immediate and broad clinical impact; Aili ranks it first and Cullis, Anderson and MacLachlan as the core.
responses.response: I take the impact seriously and keep B062 as my first alternative. My reservation is that the committee must separate the original discovery from later refinements, and here the attribution is the hardest on the shortlist. Cullis's group, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each have claims, and your trio leaves out the early encapsulation work that Sparr's trio includes. I would want that resolved before putting it first. I agree that the 2023 Medicine overlap is a framing issue and not a blocker.

responses.point: Sparr frames lipid nanoparticles as lipid self-assembly put to work, with polymorphism and pH-dependent charge translated into a platform, and proposes Cullis, Madden and Hope.
responses.response: This framing helps me, because it answers the worry that LNPs are mainly medical. If the citation is built on lipid phase behaviour and ionizable-lipid design, it is chemistry. I still doubt that Cullis, Madden and Hope alone capture the clinically decisive step, namely siRNA delivery by MacLachlan and combinatorial lipid discovery by Anderson. Our two trios do not overlap beyond Cullis, so the committee would have to decide whether the prize honours the physical chemistry or the delivery systems.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first for Buchwald and Hartwig as a bond-forming method that changed how chemists build molecules, with over 25 years of independent validation.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and attribution: two laureates is clean, and I keep B019 as an alternative. My qualification is generative potential. The 2010 cross-coupling prize already recognised the Pd-catalysis paradigm, so C-N coupling will read to many as an extension, and the Kosugi/Migita tin-amide precedent needs acknowledgement. Does the committee judge the ligand-design principle to be a distinct achievement, or a refinement of a recognised one? I am not yet convinced it is the former, which is why I rank it below degradation.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks Car-Parrinello ab initio molecular dynamics first as a very mature, unambiguously attributed game-changer for condensed-phase and reactive chemistry, and also lists base editing and degraders in his top three.
responses.response: Car-Parrinello is an excellent case on attribution and maturity, and as a physicist I find it attractive. My hesitation is only one of weighing: its impact is a method that serves other chemistry, whereas degraders opens a new class of molecular function. I note that you also place B027 third with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, which matches my revised configuration. Is your doubt on B027 only clinical timing, or the allocation?

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first for Gray and Winkler as a physically stated mechanism with decades of confirmation, and nitrogenase second while noting its catalytic mechanism is still debated.
responses.response: Gray and Winkler are physically clean and mature, which appeals to me. My question is what is the open capability, since tunnelling through proteins is now established textbook knowledge. I share your caution that phase separation is premature because the interpretation is still moving, and I would downgrade it for the same reason. On nitrogenase, an unsettled catalytic mechanism makes it hard to write a defensible citation now.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first for David Liu alone as a defined deaminase reaction turned into a general tool now entering patients, and would not stretch to a trio merely because the list supplies one.
responses.response: I agree that a single laureate is defensible if the decisive contribution is Liu's. I am less sure it is cleaner given Target-AID from Nishida and Kondo, and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes it a judgement on whether base editing is a new chemical principle or an application of that platform. Clinical data are still early, and I place it below degradation on maturity.

uncertainties: Whether a single citation should span PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues, or whether that conflates two discoveries made by different groups at different times.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto, Ciulli and Handa is contested, and Ciulli is the most notable omission.
Clinical status of degraders is from memory and not verified; no approved PROTAC drug is certain.
Whether lipid nanoparticles are judged as chemistry and whom the three names should be.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I am a Lund nanophysicist and my work on molecular motors and nanowire devices is not directly tied to any shortlisted candidate. I note that Lund colleagues Somfai and Sparr are on the committee, but I see no personal or institutional link to the nominees.
